newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens says reorganises industry units.
newsitem.headline: Siemens says reorganises industry units.

text.p: Germany's Siemens AG said on Thursday its supervisory board approved a reoganisation of its automation and industrial drives businesses.
Siemens combined the core businesses from its AUT automation and ASI drives groups to form an Automation and Drives unit, headed by ASI chief Herbert Steffen.

At the same time, AUT's postal and logistics automation businesses would become the core of a new Production and Logistics Systems group headed by AUT president Manfred von Raven. The postal operations came to Siemens in the acquisition of AEG Electrocom earlier this year.

Siemens also renamed its Industrial and Building Systems group to reflect new emphasis on services and certain industry segments. It is now called Engineering and Technical Services, but continues to be led by Konrad Pernstich.

A fourth industrial group will be formed next year after Siemens completes the acquisition of the industrial activities of Swiss energy group Elektrowatt AG. The unit will also include parts of the Industrial and Building Systems business.
In the first half of 1996/97, AUT sales fell four percent to 2.9 billion marks. Orders dropped six percent to 3.3 billion marks. It had pretax profit of 509 million marks last year.
ASI first-half sales rose two percent to 4.1 billlion marks, as orders rose two percent to 4.4 billion marks. Its pretax profit last year was 117 million marks.
ANL six-month sales were up six percent to 4.1 billion marks and orders down four percent to 4.6 billion marks. Last year it had a pretax loss of 102 million marks.
Siemens plans to report nine-month results next Monday.
